h1: Pova Residence and Boutiques Resort — a budget stay in Huai Kapi next to Big C that works as an easy-on-the-wallet base for Bangsaen and Mueang Chonburi
intro: If your Chonburi trip is all about driving yourself around, you want a clean, budget-priced room, and you don't need a pool or a sea view from the room, Pova Residence and Boutiques Resort is an option a lot of people mention among Mueang Chonburi's budget stays · it's a 2-star boutique place with about 42 rooms in the Huai Kapi area, on Soi Huai Kapi 10 in Mueang Chonburi district. What guests love most is the location, which is right next to Big C, about a 1-min walk away, close to Central Plaza Chonburi and Major Cineplex, with Bangsaen Beach about a 15-minute drive away · there's free parking, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk, and several room types including one with a balcony · prices start at about ฿590/night and review scores sit around 7.6 in the budget category, which is solid for the price.

body.html: Who Pova Residence is for — to put it as simply as possible, Pova Residence and Boutiques Resort is a place for people who want "a clean room in Mueang Chonburi at a budget price" rather than a beachfront resort experience · it's not a luxury hotel with a pool and spa, and it's not a beachfront resort where you step out of your room onto the sand · it's a 2-star boutique stay of about 42 rooms set in the Huai Kapi area on the in-town side of Chonburi, near the shopping spots and the main highway, which makes it an easy base for getting out and exploring around town and Bangsaen · what sets it apart from your average budget stay is the location right next to Big C and close to the city's main shopping centres, plus rooms that are kept cleaner than many people expect at this price · real reviews line up on this: the people who fit here best are travellers who drive themselves, people coming to handle errands or work in Mueang Chonburi, groups of friends or families doing Bangsaen on a budget, and anyone who just wants a clean room to rest up in rather than someone chasing a resort vibe or full amenities · another group that calls it worth it is people stopping over on the way to Rayong, Pattaya, or the eastern provinces who want free parking and a cheap bed for a night · you could say it plays the "budget but clean" angle well, on a budget that's easy to reach for a Chonburi trip.

Location and getting around — location is Pova Residence's main selling point, no question · the stay is at 9/31 Moo 3, Soi Huai Kapi 10, Huai Kapi, Mueang Chonburi, an area that links downtown Chonburi with the routes out to Bangsaen and Ang Sila · what guests bring up most is that it's right next to the Big C Chonburi branch, about a 1-min walk away, which makes it easy to grab food, supplies, and a quick meal without driving anywhere · nearby you also have Central Plaza Chonburi about 2–2.5 km away, and Major Cineplex less than a kilometre away for anyone who wants a movie, some shopping, or a restaurant in the mall · getting to the beach is still convenient too: about a 15-min drive gets you to Bangsaen Beach, a favourite with Bangkokians and people from the east, while Ang Sila old market, known for seafood and souvenirs, is about 4–5 km away, and you can drive on to Nong Mon Market, Khao Sam Muk, or other spots around town without much trouble · for people from Bangkok, the drive from town is about 1 hour 20 minutes to an hour and a half, and it's about 1 hour 15 minutes from Suvarnabhumi Airport · the honest caveat is that this location suits people with their own car best, because even though it's close to malls and the main road, without a car getting around the Huai Kapi area means relying mainly on songthaews, motorbike taxis, or ride-hailing apps, which at some times of day can be harder to book than in a bigger city centre · the other point is that the stay isn't beachfront, so if your main goal is walking the shore every day, you'll need to factor in the drive to and from Bangsaen each time.

"The room was cleaner than the price suggests, Big C is just a minute's walk so grabbing food is super easy, and parking is free so no worries there · Bangsaen is a quick drive away — great for budget travellers who drive themselves."

Room types and decor — Pova Residence has about 42 rooms, split into several types to suit your group size and budget · starting with the Standard Double Room, a one-big-bed room for couples or solo travellers who want a private room at a light price · and the Standard Twin Room with two single beds, good for friends or siblings who want separate beds · stepping up is the Sweet Room, a bit larger and decorated to feel a touch more special than the standards · and the one many people like best is the Deluxe Sweet Room with Balcony, which comes with a private balcony to sit out and catch the breeze — the part that gives the "boutique" in the name some meaning · the decor overall is simple and clean, in bright tones, leaning practical rather than flashy · every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, free drinking water, bathroom toiletries, and a bathroom with a shower · most real reviews agree in their praise that the rooms are clean, the beds sleep comfortably, and it's worth what you pay, with many stressing that cleanliness is a pleasant surprise for a stay at this level · but to be straight about it, some reviewers note that a few rooms or corners have a slightly musty or damp smell, especially rooms that have been closed up for a while, and a few reviews say the beds are fairly firm or don't support your back as softly as expected · these details are par for the course at budget stays and can usually be fixed by running the air conditioning to air the room out and picking a room that gets used regularly.

Amenities — let's be straight from the start: Pova Residence is a budget stay, so the amenities focus on "the essentials" rather than the luxuries · there's no pool, no fitness room, and no spa, so if those are what you're after, this may not be the answer and you should look at a resort in a higher budget · but what it does have, and what guests speak well of, is free parking, a key point for people who drive themselves since there's no worry about finding a spot or paying extra to park · there's free building-wide Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk, luggage storage, daily housekeeping, and a small common area to sit and relax · being next to Big C and near the malls means food and supplies are never a problem, since you can walk over and buy them any time · one thing to know upfront is that the building is walk-up with no lift, so if you get an upper-floor room or have heavy bags, be ready to carry your things up the stairs, or ask for a ground-floor room when you book · another point some reviews have flagged is the front desk's opening hours in practice — at certain times there may be limits on late check-in, so make your arrival time clear in advance, especially if you're arriving in the evening or late at night, to avoid issues on the spot.

Food and places to eat around the stay — the thing to understand before booking is that Pova Residence generally doesn't focus on a buffet breakfast like the big hotels, and many reviews note that breakfast isn't included in the room rate or is limited · but this is barely an issue because the location more than makes up for it · the stay is right next to Big C, a few minutes' walk away, so you can easily pick up ready-to-eat food, snacks, coffee, and groceries from the supermarket, and the Huai Kapi area also has a fair spread of made-to-order eateries, rice-and-curry shops, cafes, and convenience stores · if you want something more of a sit-down meal, drive to Central Plaza Chonburi, which has plenty of restaurants in the mall, or head over to the Bangsaen side and Nong Mon Market with their well-known seafood and snacks · for seafood lovers, the Ang Sila old market about 4–5 km away is where many people stop to buy dried squid, shrimp paste, and seafood souvenirs · all in all, food at Pova Residence isn't a reason to come and eat in-house, but the nearby malls and surrounding shops cover it well, so guests don't feel stuck on meals even though the stay has no full restaurant.

Service — service is another area that gets fairly consistent praise in real reviews for a stay at this level · several front-desk staff get mentioned as friendly, well-spoken, and helpful with all sorts of things, from check-in and check-out to recommending restaurants and sights around Mueang Chonburi and helping with parking · the front desk being open 24 hours, per the stay's information, puts people who arrive at various times more at ease · but to be straight about it, some reviews reflect that handling late-night check-in in practice has had problems — for example, one family arrived late and ran into time limits that made getting into the room awkward · that's why we recommend you give your arrival time in advance and confirm clearly with the stay, especially if you'll arrive in the evening or late · on top of that, being a small property means that when staff are thin at certain times, the response can be slower than at a big hotel, but overall service is still a point guests rate positively, and it's a part that helps lift the whole experience at this price.

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — pulling from Trip.com, Agoda, Expedia, Tripadvisor, and other booking sites, the picture that emerges is fairly consistent for a budget stay · on the praise side: budget price and good value, rooms cleaner than expected for the price, a location next to Big C and near Central Plaza Chonburi that's handy for food and supplies, free parking that suits people who drive themselves, friendly and helpful staff, a quiet, low-key atmosphere, and a short drive to Bangsaen · on the watch-out side: the most talked-about thing is that it's a walk-up building with no lift, so upper-floor rooms mean hauling bags up the stairs; some rooms have a slightly musty or damp smell from being closed up; a few rooms' beds are fairly firm or don't support your back softly; there's no pool or resort-style amenities; it isn't beachfront so you have to drive to Bangsaen; and there have been reviews that ran into late-night check-in problems · most of these gripes are "predictable" for a 2-star budget stay and can be fixed or avoided by setting the right expectations, picking a suitable room, and communicating with the stay in advance, rather than being a big problem that makes people feel it isn't worth the price.

"Stayed two nights while travelling around Chonburi — clean room, lovely staff, really cheap · the only downside was that our room was on an upper floor with no lift, so hauling the bags up was a bit tiring. Next time I'll ask for a ground-floor room instead."

Price comparison and value — the starting price for a standard room is about ฿590/night on weekdays, which is very cheap compared with stays in Mueang Chonburi and on the Bangsaen side · larger rooms like the Sweet Room and Deluxe Sweet Room with Balcony move up into roughly the ฿700–฿1,000 range depending on room type and timing · over long weekends and festivals when crowds head to Bangsaen, prices climb and rooms fill fast, but overall it still sits in the budget tier · compared with similar-level stays in the Mueang Chonburi and Bangsaen area, what makes Pova Residence especially good value is its cleanliness for the price and its location right by the shops — for people who just need a clean room to rest in and spend the whole day out, paying a low few hundred baht a night for a clean room with free parking and a walk to Big C is good value for money · if you come as a group and split the room, or use it as a stopover on the way east, the per-person, per-night cost drops even further · but understand that this value comes in the form of "a budget stay that does its job well," not value in the sense of getting full amenities cheap, because this place cuts out extras like a pool and a restaurant to keep the price down.

Good to know before booking — there are a few things that make the stay go more smoothly · one, if you have heavy bags or don't want to climb stairs, ask for a ground-floor room when you book since the building has no lift · two, if you'll arrive in the evening or late, give your arrival time and confirm check-in with the stay in advance to avoid issues with the front desk's opening hours · three, if you're worried about a musty smell, ask to run the air conditioning to air the room out and have the front desk help sort it from check-in, or ask to change rooms if needed · four, if you want breakfast, be ready for the fact that this place doesn't focus on breakfast, but you can easily walk to Big C or the nearby shops · five, this stay suits people who drive themselves best, since you make full use of the location and free parking; if you don't have a car, budget for ride-hailing to get around the area and over to Bangsaen · six, over long weekends and festivals rooms fill fast and prices climb, so book ahead, compare across several platforms, and pick free cancellation up front if your plans aren't firm yet.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Pova Residence and Boutiques Resort is the best fit for travellers who drive themselves, people who want a clean room at a budget price in Mueang Chonburi, and people using the stay as just a base for getting out to Bangsaen and around town · its location next to Big C and near Central Plaza Chonburi, the free parking, the well-kept clean rooms, and prices starting in the low few hundred baht make it good value as a budget stay — to the point where it's not easy to find a rival in the area that offers this level of cleanliness at the same price · if you're after a beachfront resort with a pool, a buffet breakfast, or full amenities to lounge around the property all day, this isn't the answer, and you should look at resorts on the Bangsaen or Pattaya beach side in a higher budget instead · but for a drive-yourself Chonburi trip where you want to save on the room to keep your budget for eating and sightseeing — Pova Residence is an option that does its job well and gives good value, and it's the reason so many budget travellers choose to stay here again when they're back in Chonburi.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Pova Residence and Boutiques Resort

faq.q: Where is Pova Residence and Boutiques Resort · what's nearby?
faq.a: The stay is at 9/31 Moo 3, Soi Huai Kapi 10, Huai Kapi, Mueang Chonburi · the highlight is that it's right next to the Big C Chonburi branch, about a 1-min walk away, near Major Cineplex and Central Plaza Chonburi (~2–2.5 km) · about a 15-min drive to Bangsaen Beach and about 10 minutes to Ang Sila old market · it's about 1 hour 15 minutes from Suvarnabhumi Airport.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Pova Residence · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿590/night for a Standard Double Room on weekdays · there's a Standard Twin Room (~฿650), Sweet Room (~฿790), and Deluxe Sweet Room with Balcony (~฿990) · over long weekends and festivals prices climb and rooms fill fast, so compare several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Pova Residence best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers who drive themselves, people who want a clean room at a budget price in Mueang Chonburi, and people using the stay as a base for Bangsaen and around town · it suits budget trips and stopovers on the way to the eastern provinces · it isn't a fit for people who want a beachfront resort, a pool, or a buffet breakfast.

faq.q: Does Pova Residence have a pool and a lift?
faq.a: There's no pool and it's a walk-up building with no lift · if you have heavy bags or can't easily climb stairs, we recommend asking for a ground-floor room when you book · what it does have is free parking, free building-wide Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk, and daily housekeeping.

faq.q: Does Pova Residence have breakfast · where can you eat around the stay?
faq.a: The stay doesn't focus on breakfast and at times breakfast isn't included in the room rate · but this is barely an issue because Big C is a 1-min walk away, so you can easily buy ready-to-eat food, coffee, and snacks · the Huai Kapi area also has rice-and-curry shops, made-to-order eateries, and cafes, and you can drive to eat at Central Plaza or over on the Bangsaen side, which aren't far.

faq.q: What should you know about check-in at Pova Residence?
faq.a: Check-in is at 2:00 PM and check-out at 12:00 PM, and the front desk is open 24 hours per the stay's information · but there have been reviews that ran into limits on late-night check-in, so we recommend you give your arrival time and confirm with the stay in advance, especially if you'll arrive in the evening or late, to avoid issues on the spot.
